$comment: Entry schema for contributes.terminalProfiles (process plugins that declare the shell capability, manifest apiVersion 2). Host validation lives in backend/plugin/contrib_terminal_profiles.go (install) and terminal_profiles_launch.go (launch): command is exactly one of ${pluginRoot}/<relative> (resolved symlink-safely inside the plugin, a regular executable file), a bare program name found on the login PATH, or an absolute path without '..'; '${...}' in args, env values and cwd may only be ${workspaceFolder}, ${userHome} or ${pluginRoot}; env names on the contract denylist (case-insensitive, including the denied prefixes LD_, DYLD_, GIT_, BASH_FUNC_, NPM_CONFIG_, PIP_, MINCODE_) are rejected at install and again at launch; text must be single-line without control or bidirectional override characters. Every first launch and every launch after the resolved command, args, env, cwd or plugin executable changed needs an explicit user confirmation.
description: Terminal profiles: named launchers in the terminal + menu that run a program in a new terminal pane after the user confirms the exact command line.

title.description: Menu and pane title; shown labelled as plugin-supplied.

icon.description: One of the host view icons (same set as contributes.views icon).

command.description: ${pluginRoot}/<relative path> (the executable's sha256 is part of the confirmed fingerprint), a bare program name such as "python3", or an absolute path. No shell runs in between: $VAR stays literal.

args.description: Arguments passed verbatim (after variable expansion); at most {{limits.argsTotalBytes}} bytes in total.

env.description: Extra environment variables. Names that change program loading or shell startup (PATH, LD_*, DYLD_*, NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONPATH, ...) are rejected.

cwd.description: Working directory: a variable optionally followed by a relative path. Defaults to ${workspaceFolder} (the user's home when no workspace folder is open).

platforms.description: Operating systems the profile is offered on; defaults to all. On Windows the executable must be an .exe or .com file.
